title: Almonds vs. pistachios: protein, fiber, and calories

seo.title: Almonds vs. pistachios: protein, fiber, calories
seo.meta_description: Almonds and pistachios both provide about 6 g protein per ounce. Almonds have slightly more fiber; pistachios have slightly fewer calories and more potassium.
seo.search_intent: Compare almonds and pistachios for protein, fiber, calories, fat and key micronutrients using equal serving sizes.

excerpt: Almonds and pistachios are closer nutritionally than their reputations suggest. A roughly 1-ounce serving of either delivers about 6 grams of protein; almonds have a little more fiber, while pistachios come in a few calories lower.
content_html:
Almonds and pistachios are both nutrient-dense and calorie-dense nuts. When they are compared in the same form and at the same weight, protein and calorie differences are modest; the more useful distinctions are fiber and micronutrients.

Per 100 grams

NutrientRaw almondsRaw pistachios
Calories~579~560
Protein~21.2 g~20.2 g
Fat~49.9 g~45.3 g
Fiber~12.5 g~10.6 g
Potassium~733 mg~1,025 mg
Magnesium~270 mg~121 mg

Almonds provide about 1 g more protein and 1.9 g more fiber per 100 g. Pistachios provide about 19 fewer calories and roughly 292 mg more potassium.

At a 1-ounce-style serving, the gap gets tiny

A 30 g portion of almonds provides about 174 calories, 6.4 g protein, and 3.8 g fiber. The same weight of pistachios is about 168 calories, 6.1 g protein, and 3.2 g fiber.

That is only about 6 calories and 0.3 g protein apart. Choosing one because it is supposedly dramatically higher in protein does not match the actual numbers.

Almonds stand out for magnesium and vitamin E

Raw almonds contain about 270 mg magnesium per 100 g compared with roughly 121 mg in pistachios. In a 30 g serving, that is about 81 mg versus 36 mg.

Almonds also contain considerably more alpha-tocopherol, the form of vitamin E used to express vitamin E activity.

Pistachios stand out for potassium and vitamin B6

Pistachios provide just over 1,000 mg potassium per 100 g versus about 733 mg in almonds. In 30 g, that works out to about 308 mg versus 220 mg — roughly 88 mg more potassium.

Pistachios are also unusually rich in vitamin B6 for a nut.

Which has less fat?

Pistachios are around 45.3 g fat per 100 g versus roughly 49.9 g for almonds. That 4.6 g difference per 100 g shrinks to only about 1.4 g in a 30 g portion.

Both are dominated by unsaturated fats. Added oil, salt, sugar, chocolate, or seasoning can change the final product far more than the small raw-nut difference.

The practical takeaway

For protein, almonds and pistachios are essentially tied in a realistic serving. Almonds offer a little more fiber, magnesium, and vitamin E; pistachios offer slightly fewer calories, more potassium, and more vitamin B6. Rotating both gives more nutritional variety than forcing a single winner.

faq.question: Which has more protein, almonds or pistachios?
faq.answer: Almonds, but only slightly: about 21.2 g versus 20.2 g per 100 g. A 30 g serving is roughly 6.4 versus 6.1 g.

faq.question: Which has more fiber?
faq.answer: Almonds, at about 12.5 g per 100 g versus roughly 10.6 g in pistachios.

faq.question: Which has fewer calories?
faq.answer: Pistachios by a small margin: about 560 calories per 100 g versus 579 for almonds.
